title: Postal Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC M&RA
raw_text:
3.     MOS 0160, Postal Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC M&RA

    a. Summary. Postal Officers function as special staff officers and
advisors to commanders and staffs on all military postal services, support,
operations, and functions. Postal Officers manage postal operations and
postal retail services and advises regarding federal regulations governing
mail and postal affairs laws at all command levels. Postal Officers serve as
Region Postal Directors, Installation Postal Officers, Postal Quality
Assurance/Quality Control Officers, Postal Finance Officers, And Postal
Operations Officers and as members of general or executive staffs in the
operating forces, supporting establishments, and joint staffs. They formulate
plans, policies, and procedures pertaining to postal services at all levels
of the operating forces and the supporting establishment. Postal Officers
provide advice on issues related to postal affairs, coordinate with the
department of defense (DoD) and the U.S. Postal Service (USPS) for unit
addressing, mail operations, and mail transportation throughout theater of
operations. They act as region and installation official mail managers,
ensuring that the Official Mail Cost Control Program (OMCCP) operate within
DoD and federal regulations. They represent the commanding officer to the
other services, tenant activities, the DoD, and the USPS for all postal and
official mail matters. Postal Officers will not be assigned to unit level to
conduct unit postal officer functions.

       b.   Prerequisites

        (1) Have no record of derogatory or unfavorable conduct that casts
doubt on the officer's trustworthiness and honesty.

        (2) Have no history of psychiatric disorder, alcoholism, or drug
abuse unless a medical evaluation determines the condition no longer exists.

        (3) Must have experience as a Postal Clerk, MOS 0161, in order to
properly supervise postal operations and identify noncompliance, abuse, or
depredations. However, enlisted personnel with extensive management
experience and/or background in supply chain management, may serve as Postal
Officer with a favorable endorsement from a CWO4/CWO5 currently servicing as
an 0160 Postal Officer.

        (4) Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in
MCO 1040.42B, warrant officer (WO) and limited duty officer (LDO) accession
programs.

        (5) Security requirement: secret security clearance eligibility and
have favorable entrance national agency check (ENTNAC) and national agency
check (NAC) on file.

        (6) Have no convictions by court martial, UCMJ punishment for postal
related offenses within the last.

       c.   Requirements

            (1) Complete the Postal Supervisor Course (A35A8Q1), Ft Jackson, SC.



                                          1-5                        Enclosure (1)
 1104                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



        (2) Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4) within
18 months of appointment to WO.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (d), Personnel and Administration Training and Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Postmasters and Mail Superintendents 11-9131.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
